title: 真假金丝雀的博弈第6章
content_zh:
第6章 三十七平米的局

    排骨还是热的。

    李婶的手艺，我吃了十八年，闭着眼都能尝出来。八角、老抽、一丁点陈皮回甘。顾西辞坐在我的行李箱上，两条长腿伸开，背靠着我的单人床，手里拎着一瓶八块钱的啤酒。

    “许向平下午给我打了电话。”他说。

    “说什么？”

    “说他近期做的事可能牵连到我，让我看好身边的人。”他喝了一口啤酒，目光从瓶口上方扫过来，“还特意加了一句——有机会替我跟温小姐道歉。”

    “道歉？我跟他连话都没说过几句。”

    “所以我来问你。林曼如的茶会上，是不是发生了什么你没告诉我的事？”

    我把筷子放下。

    “你怀疑我藏消息？”

    “不是藏。是漏。”他看着我，语气不重，但每个字都压得很准，“你跟我说她在花房里后悔做全职太太，想开艺术空间，被许向平拦了。这段话说得太完整了，不像是一个刚认识的阔太太会对陌生人说的掏心窝子话。”

    “你觉得她故意说给我听的？”

    “我在问你。她是故意还是不小心？”

    我端起啤酒喝了一口。苦味在舌尖上炸开。林曼如那天在花房里的表情在我脑子里回放了一遍。她低头摘枯叶的动作，她说后悔时的语气，她说“别跟别人提”时的紧张。每一个细节都很真。但就是太真了。

    “她有可能是故意的。”

    “为什么这么判断？”

    “因为她说完那段话之后特意叮嘱了我一句——别跟别人提。真正不想让人传出去的话，不会说出来。她说出来再叮嘱，等于是在告诉我这句话很重要，你应该传出去。”

    顾西辞把啤酒瓶放在地上，手指在膝盖上敲了两下。

    “林曼如嫁进林家十五年，从不受重视的小女儿变成林家实际管钱的人。林子明的慈善基金是她管的，投资账户也是她说了算。许向平去年在三支基金上亏了钱，她瞒着所有人补了窟窿，用自己名下的账户。这样的人，不会在茶会上对着一个刚认识的女人哭诉自己后悔。她要对你说什么，一定是算好了你会把话传到我耳朵里。”

    “她想通过我传什么话给你？”

    “她想告诉我，她和许向平之间不是铁板一块。”他从西装内袋里掏出一张请柬，浅蓝色封面，手绘水墨兰花，“所以她周末的画廊开业，请了你和我。”

    我接过请柬翻开。林曼如的私人画廊，地址在城南的艺术园区。开业时间周六上午十点。

    “她连许向平都没告诉。”顾西辞说，“请柬直接送到顾氏前台的，封面上只写了你的名字和我。没有林家，没有许向平，没有任何关联方。她是用自己的名义在办这件事。”

    我把请柬合上。

    “她想干什么？借顾氏的招牌给自己的画廊站台？”

    “不只。她要的是站队。邀请你我，等于告诉圈子里的所有人——顾氏站在她那边。许向平一旦发现这个画廊是他老婆背着他开的，第一反应一定是查谁在支持她。查到顾氏头上，就会认为我在背后挺她。”

    “然后许向平就会跟你翻脸。”

    “对。”

Chapter 6 Thirty-seven square meters of space

    The ribs are still hot.

    I have been eating Aunt Li's cooking for eighteen years, and I can taste it with my eyes closed. Star anise, dark soy sauce, and a little tangerine peel make it sweet. Gu Xici sat on my suitcase, with his long legs stretched out and his back leaning against my single bed, holding an eight-yuan bottle of beer in his hand.

    "Xu Xiangping called me in the afternoon," he said.

    "What did you say?"

    "He said that what he has done recently may implicate me, so I should be careful about the people around me." He took a sip of beer and glanced over the mouth of the bottle. "He also specially added - apologize to Miss Wen for me when I have the opportunity."

    "Apologise? I didn't even say a few words to him."

    "So let me ask you. Did something happen at Lin Manru's tea party that you didn't tell me?"

    I put the chopsticks down.

    "Do you suspect that I am hiding information?"

    "It's not hiding. It's leaking." He looked at me, his tone was not serious, but every word was precise, "You told me that she regretted being a full-time housewife in the flower house, and wanted to open an art space, but Xu Xiangping stopped her. This sentence is too complete, and it doesn't sound like the heartfelt words a rich lady she just met would say to a stranger."

    "Do you think she told me on purpose?"

    "I'm asking you. Did she do it on purpose or accidentally?"

    I picked up the beer and took a sip. The bitter taste explodes on the tongue. Lin Manru's expression in the greenhouse that day replayed in my mind. The way she lowered her head to pick dead leaves, the tone when she said she regretted it, the nervousness when she said "don't mention it to others". Every detail is authentic. But it's just too true.

    "She might have done it on purpose."

    "Why are you so judgmental?"

    "Because after she said that, she specifically told me - don't mention it to others. If you really don't want people to spread it, you won't say it. She said it and warned me, which is equivalent to telling me that this sentence is very important and you should spread it."

    Gu Xici put the beer bottle on the ground and tapped his fingers on his knees twice.

    "Lin Manru has been married to the Lin family for fifteen years, and has gone from being an underappreciated youngest daughter to being the actual money manager of the Lin family. She manages Lin Ziming's charity fund, and she has the final say on investment accounts. Xu Xiangping lost money in three funds last year, and she made up the hole without telling everyone, using an account in her own name. Such a person will not cry about his regrets to a woman he just met at a tea party. Whatever she wants to say to you, she must have figured it out and you will pass the words to my ears."

    "What message does she want to convey to you through me?"

    "She wanted to tell me that she and Xu Xiangping are not monolithic." He took out an invitation from the inner pocket of his suit, with a light blue cover and hand-painted ink orchids. "So she invited you and me to her gallery opening this weekend."

    I took the invitation and opened it. Lin Manru's private gallery is located in the art park in the south of the city. Opening time is Saturday at 10am.

    "She didn't even tell Xu Xiangping." Gu Xici said, "The invitation was sent directly to the Gu family's front desk. Only your name and mine were written on the cover. There is no Lin family, no Xu Xiangping, and no related parties. She is doing this in her own name."

    I closed the invitation.

    "What does she want to do? Borrow Gu's sign for her own gallery platform?"

    "Not only. What she wants is to take sides. Inviting you and me is equivalent to telling everyone in the circle that Gu is on her side. Once Xu Xiangping finds out that his wife opened this gallery behind his back, his first reaction will be to find out who is supporting her. If he finds out about Gu, he will think that I am supporting her behind her back."

    "Then Xu Xiangping will fall out with you."

    "Yes."
title_en: The Game of True and False Canaries Chapter 6
